title: Control tracking sensitivity starting range
summary: For control tracking, a good starting range is about 35-45 cm/360, with slower bias for steadier readable corrections and slightly faster bias if width changes feel too heavy.
why: Viscose recommends roughly 30-50 cm/360 for most control-tracking subcategories, with slower bias helping steadier integration and precision.
Readable control tracking rewards clean, gradual corrections more than frantic reaction speed, so a slightly steadier sensitivity often fits the task.
actions: Start around 40 cm/360 and adjust slower if your path wobbles through readable strafes.
If you can read the width changes but the mouse feels too heavy to keep up, test a slightly faster step inside the same range.
Judge the setting by correction path quality first, not by whether the first few runs feel familiar.
avoid: Do not force an ultra-fast setup if the task is exposing readable correction errors.
Avoid assuming one universal number works for every control-tracking width and muscle-group emphasis.

drills.label: Control tracking sens check
drills.reason: Readable control tasks make correction quality differences between nearby sensitivities easier to spot.

evidence.claim: Most control-tracking subcategories work well around 30-50 cm/360, with some slower or faster exceptions depending on the muscle-group goal.
evidence.excerpt: For the other subcategories, I recommend anything between 30 to 50 cm.
